candidate.src_content_hash_rule: sha256 over the byte string 'openssl-rs/src-rs/v1\0' followed, for each src/**/*.rs in sorted relative-path order, by relpath\0filebytes\0

census_crosscheck.note: The census is the FROZEN Phase-25 atlas (earlier candidate). A changed file is candidate drift since that freeze, not a defect.

cohort_metrics.3_note: Obligations are discharged ONLY at the seal point (AGENTS.md §7 SAFETY_DISCHARGED, §18). No per-site validity contract has been proven for any closure file at this candidate, so this is honestly 0. A present seam is OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, which is not discharge.

4_unresolved_interior_raw_sites.note: Allocation calls and release calls are reported separately and must not be added into one 'raw site' figure. Calls in no-seam files are unambiguously unclassified interior work. Calls in seam-bearing files are mixed: they include legitimate seam-constructor/release sites and any remaining interior sites — this lightweight pass cannot separate them, so they are reported as classification burden, not as defects.

cohort_metrics.5_note: 0 by construction: no mechanism is SAFETY_DISCHARGED, so no consumer's dependency closure can be discharged. Functional re-testing is required before any graduation.

ledger_seam_crosscheck.note: Files state.json lists as converted_files_on_branch that carry NO recognised seam token in the current tree. The file-level seam heuristic therefore UNDERCOUNTS reconstruction for structural/lock-based conversions that leave no owner token.

mapping_coverage.note: src modules named by none of the nine mechanism directory rules (e.g. mac, sm2, modes, des, sm3). Their conversion work is real but is OUT of this nine-mechanism closure: a known coverage gap of this refresh, not a claim they are unconverted.

mechanism_file_mapping.rule: declared as data in atlas_refresh.py:MECHANISM_PATHS; trailing '/' = directory prefix, bare path = exact file; derived from CLOSURE.md 'authority evidence' prefixes + state.json converted_files_on_branch + PROGRESS.md

non_claims: This refresh measures ownership-reconstruction progress only; it claims no SAFETY_DISCHARGED and no SAFE_COMPATIBLE.
The 33 historical DROP_IN_PASS verdicts are against an EARLIER candidate; functional re-testing is required before graduation.
A present seam (OwnedCtx/OwnedBuf/impl Drop/…) is OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, never discharge.
Mechanism→file association is a declared directory mapping, not a per-symbol proof; it is an upper bound used for reachability.
Production allocation calls are a work-burden metric, not a defect count; allocation and release calls are reported separately.
Calls in files that also carry a seam token are classification burden, not proven defects or proven conversions.

recomputed_source_scan.allocator_definition_note: Files defining the CRYPTO_* allocator entry points (the seam itself); their calls are the seam being defined, not interior residuals, and are excluded from metric 4. Both `src/runtime/mem.rs` and `src/runtime/secure.rs` are treated as allocator seam implementations.
recomputed_source_scan.family_note: Families keep secure, cleansing, array, aligned, duplicate and realloc operations visible; they are not folded into plain malloc.
recomputed_source_scan.measurement_method: comments and string/char literals are blanked in place by a hand-written scanner (offsets and line numbers preserved); a site is an identifier followed by optional whitespace/turbofish and '(' and is not a `fn` definition; alloc/release names are discovered from the seam files; test classification covers inline cfg(test) modules, external `mod name;` files, and individual items
recomputed_source_scan.raw_site_keys_note: `raw_site_patterns`, `files_zero_raw_sites`, `files_with_raw_sites` and `raw_sites_total` are deprecated aliases. They now describe production call sites (comments/literals stripped; test and seam excluded), not the old token regex counts.
recomputed_source_scan.raw_sites_total_note: DEPRECATED ALIAS, not used as a headline. Use production_alloc_calls and production_release_calls separately; they are not interchangeable and their sum is not a defect count.
recomputed_source_scan.seam_file_label: allocator seam implementation; excluded from consumer-site counts
recomputed_source_scan.test_detection_method: cfg-attribute brace span for inline cfg(test) modules, path resolution for external `#[cfg(test)] mod name;` files, and brace/statement spans for individual cfg(test) items; not a full parser (residual limitation reported)

site_worklist.note: Per-site evidence queue: production (non-test, non-seam) alloc and release call sites only, sorted by file then line.

unknown_vs_demonstrated_failure.demonstrated_failure_note: A closure file with at least one production allocation CALL and NO ownership seam is a known-unconverted interior allocation site in a mechanism a consumer needs. This is the only class this refresh asserts as failure-shaped; it is not a functional regression.
unknown_vs_demonstrated_failure.unknown_coverage_note: Mechanism dependence is MEASURED (symbol fingerprint) for 6 families and INFERRED (linkage/surface) for 27; isync and nginx reach L7 with no fingerprint. The join speaks for 6 of 1000. Absence of a fingerprint is unknown coverage, not a pass.
